title: Black Hat Europe 2025 | Ghosts in the Stream: Exposing Lives and Devices Behind Encrypted Doors

segments.text: Uh good afternoon.
Thank you for joining our talk.
In this session, we are going to share
with you our latest results regarding a
research that we have done on the Matter
standard. Now, this is a privacy track
and originally we didn't really intend
to do a privacy-related research. We
were doing whatever, you know, a
researcher is doing anomaly detection
nowadays. And we started seeing some
patterns in encrypted traffic and we
said, "Okay, this is not right."
Basically, we have a brand new standard
with strong cryptographic protection
that is built in the device and the
standard itself. And also, we have all
these legislation in the EU that is
supposed to protect our privacy. And
then we decided that this seems to be a
very important topic. We should focus on
this direction, and this is how it all
got started. My name is Jan Gabela. I'm
a senior security researcher at
Bitdefender. I work on IoT security and
vulnerability research. I've been doing
this for more than 20 years. Now, this
is a joint effort between the Eindhoven
University of Technology and
Bitdefender.
Uh about a year ago, Christopher
contacted Bitdefender trying to find a
research topic for his master's thesis.
We had this idea on doing some anomaly

how it all got started. We also done the
anomaly detection, but we progressed
also towards this direction.

let's see how it all got started. So, if

standard. This is a rising star of IoT

builds on two main pillars,
interoperability and mandatory security.
Now, interoperability means the ability
to interconnect devices coming from
different vendors. So, you no longer

Now, mandatory security is very

aligned with several legislative
directives and is slowly becoming the
single established standard for
IoT.

devices such as contact sensors and
smart plugs. But nowadays, Matter is
also being supported by very critical
devices that you found that you find in
your house such as home routers, access
point, inverters, cameras, and more and
more and more. So, I think that in the
in the very
short term, we will see more and more

Matter. And from this perspective also,
the security standpoint is changing. In

security. I think that everybody thought

And for instance, having one
network-wise symmetric key that
everybody was the
story of the day. But nowadays, with

devices that juggle with uh

happening in the field of

it, things look very nice at least on uh
paper.

same page. Well,
okay, Matter has been a subject of
discussion at previous other briefings,
especially one taking place here last
year at Black Hat Europe. In summary,
Matter supports strong security by
encrypting the communication between
devices that are part of a security
enclave called a fabric. A fabric
essentially is just a set of devices
that share a trusted root, and devices
inside of a fabric establish session
keys via asymmetric cryptography.
But, I mean, what about privacy?
So, Matter supports the mDNS SD

network. And although some of the

security researchers.

versioning of the CASE protocol. Matter

a fabric is encrypted. So, therefore,
